audit.whatIsWrong: diff reads 'HARD' while diffRating is 4/10, tone is the green token, and report[14] calls it 'Favoured matchup'. Also the level chart sides disagree with their own why text at levels 4-5, 6 and first item.
audit.why: packet.levelChart is [Gnar, Gnar, Gnar, Skill, Skill, Gnar, Nasus] and matches whys[3] ('pure Rage RNG'), whys[4] ('just whether Mega is up') and whys[5] ('beats him before Sheen'). The stored sides say Gnar/Gnar/Skill.
audit.corrected: diff set to EASY; rows 4-5, 6 and first item flipped as one atomic group with ratings realigned (Skill rows 5/10, Gnar first-item row 7/10).

audit.whatIsWrong: The spike text never gives Wither's real cooldown, so 'trade around Wither' has no timer attached.
audit.why: Kit file: Wither is 15/14/13/12/11s at 700 range. Fifteen seconds at rank 1 is a long, concrete window in which Gnar's Hyper kiting works normally.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two decisive interactions were absent. Fury of the Sands (R) deals percent-max-health damage, so stacking raw resistances does not answer it; and Siphoning Strike (Q) is an auto-attack reset, so his burst opens on an auto wind-up, not on a visible cast.
audit.why: Riot's R text describes a battering storm with bonus Armor/MR for him and the kit flags percentHealth; the Q flag autoReset matches Riot's 'strikes his foe'. Both are flagged in _missing for this exact matchup.
audit.corrected: percent-health line added to phases[4].why; the auto-reset tell added to dosFull[2].d, which previously carried a copy-pasted Wither sentence under the title 'Deny his Q stacks'.

audit.why: Mirror audit (nasus vs gnar) already established that GNAR! only stuns on terrain contact and that Gnar's Hop bounces off units to travel further. This side's text does not contradict either; the wall condition is already stated as 'wall-bounce'/'wall-combo'.
audit.corrected: No change — restating the mirror's findings rather than re-deriving them.

edits.before: Boomerang + hop kite wins every melee matchup early. Identify how Nasus contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Mini's ranged autos plus one Boomerang win the first trade — Nasus has zero stacks and no tool to answer ranged harass.

edits.before: Rage management is the champion — track your own bar. Only take the trade when Nasus's Wither is down.
edits.after: The Hyper third-hit proc plus Boomerang chunks him at 2 — he can only walk up to last-hit a Q stack and eat it.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Nasus must walk into your range.
edits.after: Boomerang's slow and Hyper's move speed kite his step-ups, denying Q stacks on the cannon before Wither is even ranked.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Wither's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Pure Rage RNG: a full-Rage Mega Wallop wins it, but stuck in Mini with Rage down his 15s Wither and stacked Q punish you.

edits.before: Mega + R against a wall is the best engage top lane owns. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Nasus's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Fury of the Sands burns percent max health, so armour alone will not save you — at 6 the only question is whether Mega is up.

edits.before: Stridebreaker is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Wither's cooldown.
edits.after: Your Mega Wallop or GNAR! all-in still beats him before Sheen and full stacks come online.

edits.before: Two items on: your pattern is at full power. Nasus carry threat 10/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: A fully stacked Q plus Trinity and a Wither all-in outscales your form-burst — the late 1v1 is simply his.

edits.before: Nasus wastes Wither — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: His Q is an auto reset: the wind-up is your tell to step out.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Wither runs 15s at rank 1 and kills Hyper kiting — trade after it.

notes: packet.defects flags 'Spirit Visage' in spikes[3].text as a probable wrong ability name matching 'Spirit Fire'. That is a FALSE POSITIVE — Spirit Visage is a real item Nasus builds and the sentence is about itemisation, not his E. Left untouched. Separately, the mirror audit reported a fabricated name 'Quickness' on the nasus-vs-gnar page; it does not appear anywhere in gnar-vs-nasus, so nothing to fix from this side. The diff enum change HARD->EASY is proposed on the strength of diffRating 4/10, the green tone token and report[14]'s 'Favoured matchup' all agreeing against it; if the enum vocabulary uses a different token for favoured matchups, apply that token instead.
